rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Banned words — grep zero-tolerance.
Ritual / ceremony — hard ban
No stale markers, no "fixed" retrospectives, no session biography.
Register match.
Rough-cut drafts for articles.
Credit original when paraphrasing named technique.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 49: We believe the loop matters more than the model, and we built this training around that.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Author-we violation: substitute "the training authors" for "we" — sentence becomes weird. Recast as "The training pins" or passive "Loop-first framing shapes this training" to drop first-person authorial voice.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Always "you", never "the student"; teacher framing stays out of body.
Don't smuggle terms of art from maintainer into body.
Over-hedge detector.
Verbatim-frame-cite in reference artefact.
Cap practitioner attribution at one student-side mention per module.
Punchy framing keeps punch; carve-out lives downstream.
Value-prop / positioning framing belongs in sales copy + project strategy docs, NOT student-facing curriculum body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 5: This capability unlocks transformational value across your entire delivery organisation. | 37: Unlike vendor tooling that locks your team in, this approach keeps you in control of the work.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Line 5: "unlocks transformational value" is marketing language; restate as concrete benefit ("lets you read", "shows your team"). Line 37: Vendor reference + defensive framing; swap "vendor tooling" to concrete tool name or drop "unlike" comparison entirely.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Watch out for planting jargon too early.
Audit closer when trimming body-prose forcing function.
The **What happened:** block is OPTIONAL
No combative verbs about the agent in body prose.
Headers must be literally true about the mechanism.
Machine-cadence fat — the shape of good prose without the content.
Don't state a count the adjacent list already holds.
A slogan that is false as stated is not punchy framing — run the truth test before reaching for §12.
A claim binds to every body that states it, not just the one holding the stamp.
A rule set reconstructed at session start goes stale inside the session — re-derive it per target, not per sweep.
One doc per scarce-attention audience; delta-only.
Trainer-facing text is self-contained.
A sentence saying how you'd know points at the outcome, not the nearest artifact.
Aspirational destination, never corrective gap.
Earn every technical term on first use.
Business-audience word ban (Agents 101 default).
Memory vs context — use deliberately.
Forcing functions shape behavior — name them, don't hide them.
Live artifact, not a summary or a log.
Preamble teaches; body proves.
Teach a mechanic, not a role.
Connections question holds a real question, not a rhetorical one.
Lectures fire on arrival, not in retrospect.
Each exercise uses one forcing function and no more than one debrief beat.
Inside fenced prompts the rules live in a different register.
Careless cross-module refs create dead-end students.
Precision costs words that felt soft; earn them.
Jargon as obstacle vs. tool.
Keep instruction mechanical, not motivational.
Reference first; then opinion.
Test before ship — write test-shaped feedback into a student run.
Tool-agnostic when the tool is swappable; tool-named when it is load-bearing.
Failure-recovery beats teach the move twice; catch the second teach.
Agendum vs. outcome.
No forced-march pace constraint.
On practitioner vocabulary and readability.
Debrief shape — three clauses.
Pat-on-the-back closer is banned; full stop.
How-you-know points at outcome, not artifact.
Connections paragraph optional; when present, carve-out from context-vs-voice rules.
The Big Idea is load-bearing for the module's mood arc — no placeholder generalisations.
Affordance detail at moment of use.
Pre-prompt checks must be plausibly-failable.
Architecture-naming convention — preserve per-training constants.
Trainer notes stay below `<!-- maintainer -->`.
Student-team voice in fenced code + example artifacts only.
Hard-gate — each exercise tests something.
Backwards-compat on terminology splits — hold the old term when students carry the question.
Each prompt must be copyable (in Antti's hands, the whole block).
Prompt bodies use imperative.
Run the prompt-body as a standalone unit before landing it.
Prompt decision points are scoped: output shape, model, mode, connectors, platform.
User-facing prompts use second person and imperative; ask for artifacts and decisions.
No jargon; no product name before positioning.
Buyer problem first; product second.
Status quo cost must be explicit.
Proof >> persuasion.
CTAs are concrete, not motivational.
Module file Big Idea lands strategyframe in concrete terms.
Key Concepts names the level of analysis the module operates at.
Module reference pages do not invent strategy.
Mood-arc target lives in AE101's Content Strategy resource (bosser-strategy skill), not body maintainer notes.

findings.quote: We believe the loop matters more than the model, and we built this training around that.
findings.harm: Author-we in body prose refers to training authors rather than students or the training itself as subject, creating first-person-plural voice that violates the student-centric perspective contract. The rule prevents cult-of-personality framing and ensures body prose addresses the student's action, not the author's intent.
findings.fix: Recast as impersonal training-as-subject (e.g., "The training emphasizes loop over model") or as a teaching principle without author voice (e.g., "The loop matters more than the model"). Drop "believe" flourish when recasting.

findings.quote: We believe the loop matters more than the model, and we built this training around that.
findings.harm: Author-we violation under the author-name sub-rule of Rule 6. First-person-plural voice referring to "we built this training" is training-as-organisation framing. This binds the teaching to the creators rather than to the student's practice, ages poorly when other trainers deliver, and violates the anti-cult-of-personality principle.
findings.fix: Recast to second-person ("your" framing of the loop) or impersonal ("The loop shapes this training"). When removing we, audit for editorial flourish carrier ("believe") and drop alongside.

findings.quote: This capability unlocks transformational value across your entire delivery organisation.
findings.harm: Value-prop / positioning framing in student-facing body. The phrase "unlocks transformational value" is aspirational marketing language that belongs in sales copy or strategy docs, not in teaching prose. It reads defensive and treats the student as needing reassurance rather than offering substance and evidence.
findings.fix: Replace with concrete benefit tied to what student will do: e.g., "Reading your team's field conventions shapes how you draft close-outs" or drop the flourish entirely and open directly on the mechanism.

findings.quote: Unlike vendor tooling that locks your team in, this approach keeps you in control of the work.
findings.harm: Value-prop / positioning leak with vendor reference. Rule 13 flags vendor-named phrases as automatically pulling marketing-vs-practitioner framing into teaching beats, because project positioning is defined against vendor stories. The "unlike vendor" construction is defensive comparison, not teaching. Importing the positioning posture into the beat distracts from the mechanics the student needs.
findings.fix: Drop the vendor comparison entirely; if the point is control, state it directly: "You stay in control by reading your team's rules off their tracker" or name the concrete tool instead of abstract "vendor tooling".
